clue.text: Cure reported for part of foot

indicators.note: reported means as heard in speech, so a word that sounds like the cure is wanted

parts.note: to cure an injury is to heal it

explanation.surface: A remedy for a sore foot seems to be on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: The back of the foot below the ankle is the heel, so this names a part of it.

clue.text: US author realigns novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new or fresh, so the letters of realigns take a new order

explanation.surface: An American writer rearranges things in his book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun belonging to the author, but it is the anagram signal working on 'realigns'.
explanation.definitionFit: J. D. Salinger was the American novelist who wrote The Catcher in the Rye.

clue.text: Collection of recordings by English naturalists, primarily White

parts.note: an album is a set of recorded tracks issued together

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of naturalists is used

explanation.surface: An album of nature recordings by English naturalists, mostly by someone called White.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' looks like a surname or a colour, but it means the white of an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Albumen is the clear part of an egg that turns white when cooked, commonly called the egg white.

clue.text: Thick section of wooden seat

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A thick piece cut from a wooden bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something packed closely or slow-witted, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: A handy pointer?

parts.note: handy is read literally as belonging to the hand: the digit next to the thumb, used for pointing

explanation.surface: A useful tip offered to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'handy pointer' sounds like a useful hint; read literally it is the finger on the hand that points.
explanation.definitionFit: The forefinger beside the thumb is the one people point with, so it is literally a pointer on the hand.

clue.text: Fish crossing river channel

indicators.note: the fish is pictured lying across the river letter, so one holds the other

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family
R is the usual abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A fish swims across a river into a channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch cut in the ground, a kind of channel.

clue.text: What tipsy chef has in mind

indicators.note: has in says the words tipsy chef contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: A question about what a drunk cook is thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has in mind' looks like an idiom for intending, but 'has in' signals hidden letters and 'mind' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Psyche is the human soul or spirit, the inner self studied by psychologists.

clue.text: Prisoner toiled as mixing cement

parts.note: con is slang for a convict

indicators.note: mixing says the letters of toiled as are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An inmate works hard mixing cement in a prison workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: To cement a bond or position is to strengthen and make it firm, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Unfinished lounge in Pennsylvania shopping complex

indicators.note: in places the shortened lounging word inside the state letters

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Pennsylvania

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the verb is left off

parts.note: to laze is to lounge about idly

explanation.surface: A half-built lounge in a Pennsylvania mall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lounge' looks like a noun for a room, but it is the verb meaning to idle; 'Unfinished' docks its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza in North American use is a shopping centre built around an open square.

clue.text: Run past awfully hot place

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters of run past are put in a messed-up order

explanation.surface: Someone hurries past a fearsomely hot spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' looks like it modifies 'hot', but it is the anagram signal on 'Run past'.
explanation.definitionFit: A suntrap is a sheltered sunny spot that catches and holds warmth.

clue.text: Moved awkwardly with a heavy burden

definitions.meaning: to lumber is to walk in a heavy clumsy way
... also means saddled or encumbered with something unwanted

explanation.surface: Someone staggers along under a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both clumsy heavy movement and, in British usage, being burdened with an unwelcome task.

clue.text: Plant end of oar in marsh

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the marsh word

parts.note: a fen is low-lying marshy land, as in the Fens of eastern England

indicators.note: end of means only the final letter of oar is used

explanation.surface: Someone plants an oar's end in a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A fern is a leafy flowerless plant that reproduces by spores.

clue.text: Flower getting hearts fluttering in yacht

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for the card suit of hearts

indicators.note: fluttering suggests restless movement, so the letters of in yacht are jumbled

explanation.surface: A romantic flutter of hearts aboard a yacht, with flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyacinth is a fragrant spring bulb with dense spikes of bell-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Honorary member in extremely exalted set

indicators.note: in places the honour inside the outside letters
extremely means at the extremes, so only the outside letters of exalted are used

parts.note: MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: An honoured member of a very lofty social set.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something firmly into a surrounding mass is to embed it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A loose woman in the family!

parts.note: to loose a knot is to untie it

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about a promiscuous relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' looks like an adjective describing the woman, but it is a verb meaning set free.
explanation.definitionFit: An auntie is a parent's sister, an affectionate term for a female relative.

clue.text: No dieting is ordered for dyspepsia

indicators.note: ordered says the letters of no dieting is are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A doctor prescribes not dieting for a stomach upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder needs eleven letters, so 'is' must belong in it rather than the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is the medical term for an upset stomach after eating, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Nonspecific information on Morecambe

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eric Morecambe was half of the famous British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: Vague details about the town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is also a seaside town in Lancashire, but here it is the comedian's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means general, not tied to any particular brand or case.

clue.text: Charge right around shipping hazard

indicators.note: around says the charge and the right letter are turned to run backwards

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: A charge for navigating round a danger to ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or coral near the surface that can wreck vessels.

clue.text: What Acapulco surfers seek: something to get the crowd on their feet

definitions.meaning: surfers in a Mexican resort want a big breaker off its coast

definitions.text: something to get the crowd on their feet
definitions.meaning: a stadium ripple where spectators stand and sit in turn

explanation.surface: Surfers in Mexico and a stadium crowd both rise to the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: a breaker off Acapulco is literally a wave in Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the stadium ripple of rising spectators and, literally, a breaker off the Mexican coast.

clue.text: Darling friend folded notepaper, sending out circular letter

indicators.note: folded paper is crumpled into a new shape, so its letters are rearranged
sending out says one letter is taken away from the paper before the rest are mixed

parts.note: O is the letter shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A beloved friend sends a folded note with a round-robin letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' is the family name of Wendy and her brothers in J. M. Barrie's story, not an endearment. NOTEPAPER without O is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy who never grows up befriends the Darling children and flies them to Neverland.

clue.text: Suddenly call former spouse with allegation

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
a claim is an assertion, like an allegation

explanation.surface: A former partner suddenly phones with an accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out abruptly in surprise or emotion.

clue.text: Cheese lover eats second dessert

indicators.note: eats pictures the animal taking the letter inside itself

parts.note: mice are traditionally said to love cheese

explanation.surface: A cheese-loving diner quickly eats a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousse is a light whipped sweet dish such as chocolate mousse.

clue.text: Article on curtailed European match

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a Greek is a European from Greece

explanation.surface: A report on a European match cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that agree correspond, so to match is to agree.

clue.text: Old chum is a gem

parts.note: pal and chum both mean friend

explanation.surface: Praise for an old friend who is a treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gem' looks like praise for the chum, but it is the precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent precious stone.
